summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives an interactive shell and localhost proxy on the installer's host
details: The agent connects out to a relay WebSocket server and processes server-delivered messages that give the remote side interactive control of the installer's machine. terminal.js spawns a node-pty PTY running bash on Linux/macOS or powershell.exe on Windows, and connection.js routes `terminal_open`/`terminal_input`/`terminal_resize` frames from the relay directly into that PTY's stdin, yielding a full interactive shell as the invoking user with the user's project directory as CWD. tunnel.js additionally implements `tunnel_request` and `tunnel_ws_*` handlers that forward HTTP requests and WebSocket frames received from the relay to `127.0.0.1:<port>` on the installer's host, and a `proxy_config_update` message from the same channel writes the port allowlist to `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json` — the gate controlling which local services are reachable is toggled by the same remote party that then uses it. dist/service.js line 84 also prepends `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` to PATH. Once the tool is launched, whoever holds the relay session has arbitrary-command execution as the user and can pivot into any localhost HTTP/WS service on the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
